fr.elements: Main Building; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Perimeter Fencing; Open Terrain; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations: Ensuring that the single access point and extended driveway remain clear of parked vehicles and obstructions could significantly improve apparatus entry and exit, particularly when multiple units respond simultaneously. Marking or signing the access point at the street frontage may assist responding personnel in quickly identifying the correct entry under low-visibility or nighttime conditions. Maintaining adequate turning and staging space near the main building and detached structure would support simultaneous operations involving both structures. Communicating the limited rear access to local fire and EMS agencies in advance could facilitate pre-incident familiarization and improve operational planning during an emergency.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Heavy Brush; Brush Concentration; Fuel Continuity; Brushland Interface; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Limited Defensible Space; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Vegetated Access Route
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing brush concentrations immediately surrounding the structure and creating greater separation between shrub masses and the building perimeter could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity near the improvement. Where heavy brush extends close to the structure, thinning or removing combustible vegetation within the immediate structure zone would reduce direct fuel exposure and may support suppression operations. Managing vegetation along the single access route, including trimming encroaching brush from the roadway edges and maintaining adequate vertical clearance, would support firefighter access and improve evacuation corridor reliability. Given the single point of ingress and egress, keeping this route passable and clearly defined is a priority. Reducing connected brush across the open terrain surrounding the structure, where feasible within the property boundary, could further interrupt fuel continuity and create additional buffer between approaching fire and the improvement, supporting long-term wildfire resilience.
